q: 1. *One metric horse power is equal to
explain: One metric horsepower (PS) is approximately 0.7355 kW, commonly rounded to 0.736 kW.

q: 2. In which of the following works, the work turned in cu. m per mason per day will be the least
options: random rubble masonry in lime mortar
explain: Stone arch work involves precise cutting, dressing, and fitting of voussoirs, making it the most labour-intensive and slowest, giving the least output per mason per day.

q: 3. In which of the following works, the work turned out in cu. m per mason per day will be the least
options: random rubble masonry in lime mortar
explain: Stone arch work requires precise dressing, shaping, and fitting of stones, making it the slowest and most labour-intensive, hence giving the least daily output per mason.

q: 4. One metric horse power is equal to
explain: One metric horsepower (HP) is defined as equal to 0.736 kilowatts.

q: 5. A document containing detailed description of all the items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: A Schedule of Rates (SOR) lists item descriptions and their current unit rates but does not specify quantities for any particular project.

q: 6. The approximate cost of the complete labour as a percentage of the total cost of the building is
explain: As a general rule of thumb in building estimation, labour cost is taken as approximately 25% of the total building cost.

q: 7. The quantum of work of any item a skilled labour is supposed to turnout in a day is known as
explain: Task work is the defined quantity of work that a skilled labourer is expected to complete within a standard working day.

q: 8. *Contractor profit is added to
explain: Contractor's profit is included during the rate analysis phase for individual items.

q: 9. The overheads and profit claimed by the contractor to client is
explain: These costs are not billed separately but are embedded into the unit rates of the work items.

q: 10. *The chairman of material rate fixation committee in district is
explain: In the Nepalese administrative system, the Chief District Officer (CDO) chairs the committee that fixes district material rates.

q: 11. Rate analysis prepared by ministry of transport and work includes
explain: According to the MOPIT (Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport) norms, rate analysis comprehensively includes the cost of labour, materials, and necessary equipment/machinery for the task.

q: 12. The expected out turn of half brick partition wall per mason per day is
explain: A half-brick wall, being measured in area (m²) rather than volume, has an expected mason output of about 4.0 m² per day.

q: 13. In sanitary pipe line for 3m length, how many skilled labour are required
explain: Higher grade concrete (M20) requires more effort; the norms specify 3 skilled and 30 unskilled workers for this volume.

q: 14. The no. of masons required per cubic metre of DRY stone masonry (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: Dry stone masonry is labor-intensive; 0.8 masons are required per cubic meter.

q: 15. The no. of skilled man power required per cubic metre cement concrete 1:2:4 (as per MOPIT norms), is
explain: For mixing and placing 1:2:4 concrete, the skilled labor coefficient is 0.2 per cubic meter.

q: 16. In RCC work, one mason in one day can perform
explain: In reinforced cement concrete (RCC) work, the out-turn per mason is relatively low (0.20 m3) due to the complexity of working around reinforcement.

q: 17. When a contractor is paid certain percentage over the actual cost of the construction as his profit, such contract is termed as
explain: A cost-plus-percentage contract pays the contractor the actual construction cost plus an agreed percentage as profit margin.

q: 18. *The number of skilled manpower required for fabrication of 1MT steel is
explain: Fabricating one metric ton (MT) of reinforcement steel typically requires 12 skilled workers.

q: 19. The term VAT stands for
explain: VAT stands for Value Added Tax, a consumption tax levied at each stage of value addition in the supply chain.

q: 20. *The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: The standard bulk density for Portland cement used in calculations is 1440 kg/m3.

q: 21. 1 Dharni weight equal to
explain: The traditional Nepali unit of weight, 1 Dharni, is equal to approximately 2.4 kg.

q: 22. The work charged establishment in Nepalese context is
explain: As per Nepalese practice, the work-charged establishment cost is provided at 1.5% of the project cost.

q: 23. Contractor tax is
explain: In many South Asian public procurement systems, a 1.5% TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) is applied to the contractor's bills.

q: 24. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having certain relationship with real damage, is known as
explain: Unliquidated damages are not fixed in the contract and are determined by a court based on the actual loss suffered.

q: 25. When engineering departments undertake the works of other departments the amount charged toward design, supervision and execution etc. is called
explain: Centage charges (or departmental charges) are fees collected by a construction department for services rendered to another department.

q: 26. Which of the following is known as job overhead?
explain: Job overheads are expenses directly related to a specific project site, such as insurance for workers and site-specific supervision.

q: 27. Costs which are independent of output and no alternation by the change in production level are called
explain: Fixed costs remain constant regardless of the level of output or production, unlike variable costs which change with production volume.

q: 28. Actual Cost of construction plus certain profit is paid to the contractor . such a contract is known as
explain: Surface dressing involves cleaning the site by removing grass, vegetation, and leveling minor undulations up to a depth of 15 cm.

q: 29. Rate analysis is based on the following factors
explain: Analysis of rates considers the quantity of materials, their quality, current market rates, and labor costs to determine the unit price of an item.

q: 30. In general for analysis of rates the reduction in volume of wet mixed mortar over the sum total volume of ingredient material is taken as
explain: When dry ingredients (cement + sand) are mixed and wetted to form mortar, the resulting volume reduces due to voids being filled; this reduction is standardly taken as 25% in rate analysis.

q: 31. The defect liability period in construction norms for rate analysis is
explain: As per standard construction norms for rate analysis, the defect liability period (during which the contractor is responsible for rectifying defects) is 1 year.

q: 32. FIDIC is
explain: FIDIC (Fédération Internationale Des Ingénieurs-Conseils) is the International Federation of Consulting Engineers.

q: 33. Key components of norms prepared for rate analysis of works may not include with quantity of
explain: Establishment costs (overhead) are added as a percentage, not as a specific quantity component in the base norms.

q: 34. The rates worked for material/labour based on paid bills/vouchers produced by contractor plus profit is
explain: Star rates are rates derived from actual market prices plus profit when the item is not in the standard schedule of rates.

q: 35. The expected out turn of cement concrete 1 : 2 : 4 per mason per day is
explain: As per standard output norms, laying 1:2:4 cement concrete gives an expected mason output of about 5.0 m³ per day.

q: 36. The rate of an item of work depends on
explain: The rate of any item of work is influenced by the specifications of the work itself, the quality/specification of materials used, and the mix proportion of mortar/concrete -- all together determine cost.

q: 37. In analysis of rates, contractor profit is taken at the rate of
explain: As established earlier, contractor's profit in standard rate analysis is conventionally taken at 10% of the total cost.

q: 38. While analyzing the rates, water charges are added on those items, which require water in construction and these charges are added at the rate of
explain: Water charges (for construction items requiring water, like concrete/masonry) are added in rate analysis at 1.5% of the relevant cost.

q: 39. While doing analysis of rate, the number of bricks taken into account per cubic metre is
explain: As established earlier, 500 bricks per cubic metre of masonry is the standard figure used in rate analysis calculations.
